'''Ndamba or "Chindamba"''' is classified as a [[Bantu language]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Tense and Aspect in Bantu|last=Nurse|first=Derek|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2008|isbn=9780199239290|location=United States}}</ref> It is one of 87 languages spoken in [[Tanzania]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Legere|first=Karsten|year=2002|title=The "Languages of Tanzania" project: background, resources, and perspectives|url=http://www.sprak.gu.se/digitalAssets/1324/1324043_the-languages-of-tanzania-project.pdf|journal=Africa & Asia|volume=2|pages=163–186|archive-date=2015-07-31|access-date=2017-01-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150731181208/http://sprak.gu.se/digitalAssets/1324/1324043_the-languages-of-tanzania-project.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Most Chindamba speakers are bilingual in [[Swahili language|Swahili]] and Chindamba.<ref>{{cite book |title=A Grammatical Sketch of Chindamba - A Bantu Language (G52) of Tanzania|last1=Edelsten |first1=Peter |last2=Lijongwa Kipandula |first2=Chiku|year=2010 |isbn=978-3-89645-706-6|page=11|publisher=Rüdiger Köppe Verlag}}</ref>

The other two [[language]]s most similar to Ndamba are [[Mbunda language|Mbunga]] and [[Pogolo language|Pogolo]], because all of them belong to the same [[Language family|language group]], which are the [[Kilombero languages|Kilombero]] languagues.<ref>[[Kilombero languages]]</ref>
